population: The frozen eligible list of reproducible, license-verified Python repair tasks qualified on native Linux x86_64; the list is currently empty and cannot be frozen.
primary_endpoint: For each eligible task and condition, 1 only when independent functional validation passes and the frozen architecture profile reports no newly introduced forbidden violation; otherwise 0, including timeout or method failure. Compare paired task-level proportions.
secondary_endpoints: reported input/output tokens and dated-price estimated cost when a provider is approved
pairing: Pair conditions within task and seed; aggregate repetitions within task before cross-task inference.
missingness: Timeouts and method failures are primary failures; infrastructure failures are missing, reported by category, and included in worst/best-case sensitivity analyses.
stopping: No optional stopping. Stop only at prespecified resource, safety, or per-run timeout limits; do not replace failed selected tasks.
retry_policy: No outcome-based retry. One infrastructure retry is permitted only when the first attempt produced no task outcome, and both attempts remain recorded.
confirmatory_tests: Use the exact McNemar test for paired binary primary outcomes and report paired risk difference and matched odds ratio. Use task-level paired bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. Use Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for prespecified skewed continuous paired outcomes only when tie and symmetry diagnostics permit; otherwise report paired bootstrap intervals and descriptive effects.
multiplicity: Apply Holm correction across the prespecified secondary confirmatory hypothesis family; label all other analyses exploratory.
robustness: Report complete-case plus worst/best-case missingness sensitivity, project-cluster bootstrap, seed-level stability, and the four prespecified ablations.
exclusions: Apply immutable-revision, license, resource, source-layout, submodule, evaluator, and Linux x86_64 eligibility rules before method outcomes are available.
environment: Pin repository revisions, dependency lock, Python version, OCI image digest, native linux/amd64 platform, provider/model/version, configuration, and action commits in evidence.
amendments: A material change requires a new protocol version and new human approval; retrospective endpoint changes are forbidden.
